hero.headline: F-bombs fly in confrontation over Port St. Lucie campaign signs
hero.teaser: A profanity-laced confrontation was captured on video between mayoral challenger Steve Giordano and the husband of incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin.
hero.body:
As the August election approaches, tensions are rising between the two political camps as incumbent Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin faces challenger Steve Giordano in the race for mayor. The incidents prompted the Port St. Lucie Police Department to launch investigations into two separate cases involving campaign signs, one of which led to a confrontation.

 During the overnight hours Friday, Aug. 7, Giordano told CBS12 News that he and his campaign manager were putting up signs near Southwest Airoso Boulevard and Southwest Thornhill Drive. Giordano said he saw a man remove a sign from the ground and throw it. Giordano then grabbed his cellphone and began recording the encounter.

 The man appears to be Shannon Martin's husband, Aaron Martin, a lieutenant with the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Video shows a profanity-laced confrontation between Giordano and Martin, with the two shouting at each other and making accusations about campaign signs being placed in the community without property owners' permission.

 Police said investigators learned that one homeowner had given permission for one campaign sign to be placed on the property, while another resident of the home, who has limited English proficiency, told members of the opposing campaign they could also place a sign there. Investigators said the language barrier contributed to the confrontation over the campaign signs and whether the previously placed sign could be moved or removed. At this time, police said there is no indication that any campaign signs involved in the incident were stolen or intentionally damaged.

cards.headline: Indian River County approves expansion of Westside Racquet Club in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Commission approved a special exception use and Phase 1 site plan on August 4 for the renovation and expansion of the Westside Racquet Club, a 1970s-era fac
cards.body:
The Indian River County Commission approved a special exception use and Phase 1 site plan on August 4 for the renovation and expansion of the Westside Racquet Club, a 1970s-era facility in Vero Beach that has fallen into disrepair in recent years. The 6.89-acre property is located east of 43rd Avenue Southwest, north of 6th Lane Southwest and south of Fifth Place Southwest.

 Phase 1 of the project will restore the existing eight tennis courts, construct four new padel courts and construct associated site improvements including utilities, stormwater, parking and landscaping. The existing 2,400-square-foot clubhouse will be restored in Phase 2, which will also add two padel courts. Phase 3 will include a pool house and four pickleball courts, while Phase 4 will add two additional tennis courts. The Planning Zoning Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval on June 11 but added a special condition due to concerns about potential noise pollution and light infiltration onto adjacent properties.

 Vice-Chairwoman Laura Moss expressed concerns about voting on the special exception use that would cover all four phases while only approving the Phase 1 site plan, saying commissioners were being asked to vote in the blind. She also raised concerns about pickleball noise and lighting impacts on neighboring residents. Planning Development Services Director John Stoll said the county can require traffic studies once the project exceeds 400 average daily trips and can implement noise mitigation measures including limiting nighttime lighting and operational hours, requiring special paddles and balls, and increasing separation from neighbors.

 District 3 Commissioner Joseph Earman pointed out the continuity of use on the parcel and said he had heard from residents who think the improvements will add value to their property. Mark Jaffe, a 4th Lane Southwest resident, was the only public speaker and said he would like to see the project move forward. The County Commission voted unanimously to approve the requests.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie postpones Riverland sports complex rezoning after Tradition residents protest
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously on July 27 to postpone a rezoning request for a 135,000-square-foot indoor and outdoor sports recreation complex in the Riverland
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously on July 27 to postpone a rezoning request for a 135,000-square-foot indoor and outdoor sports recreation complex in the Riverland area after dozens of Tradition-area homeowners packed City Chambers in protest. The council tabled the request from Riverland/Kennedy II LLC until August 24 to give the developer time to hold a neighborhood meeting with concerned residents. The developer GL Homes is seeking to rezone approximately 33.23 acres south of Southwest Discovery Way and east of Southwest Sundance Vista Boulevard from St. Lucie County Agricultural to Riverland-West Sports Recreation Master Planned Unit Development.

 Residents who spoke at the hearing said they purchased their homes with the understanding that the parcel would be a city park, not a commercial recreation facility. Southwest River Rock Road resident Jim Riordan told the council GL Homes has 1,300 other acres where they could build the complex and that the company is already advertising the fitness center in sales materials for new parcels.

 Harriet Gallas said she was told when she bought her house there would be a park over the berm next to her property. She told the council the planned 72 pickleball courts, bocci courts, tennis courts, dog park and RV park would destroy her quality of life through noise pollution.

 Planning Zoning Director Mary Savage-Dunham told the council the rezoning is consistent with the city comprehensive plan and a pre-existing Development of Regional Impact for the area. The site is designated Neighborhood Village Commercial, which allows a mixture of residential and non-residential uses including commercial offices, personal and household services, institutional facilities, public facilities, parks, playgrounds and similar services. Land Use Attorney Azlina Goldstein, representing the applicant, initially resisted postponing the request and said details about landscaping, buffers and specific indoor and outdoor features would be addressed during the site-plan process, not the rezoning.

 Mayor Shannon Martin asked Goldstein if GL Homes would be willing to meet with residents to address their concerns. Vice-Mayor Jolien Caraballo urged Goldstein to table the request, saying residents did not comprehend the quasi-judicial rezoning process. After loud protest from the audience, the council voted to postpone the hearing until August 24. City Attorney Richard Berrios explained that the rezoning is a quasi-judicial process limited to sworn testimony and facts applied to the specific rezoning request, with details about landscaping and specific features reserved for the site-plan process.

cards.headline: State lawmaker challenges Fort Pierce Causeway Cove development over zoning compliance
cards.teaser: State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of the Live Local Act, raising questions about the massive waterfront project.
cards.body:
State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of Florida's Live Local Act, the same law she supported in 2023 that allows developers to bypass local height and density restrictions. The Causeway Cove project would transform the existing Causeway Cove Marina into a mixed-use development featuring more than 900 apartments and condos, restaurants, and a hotel tower reaching nearly 200 feet in height.

 Trabulsy said a mapping error incorrectly designated portions of the Causeway Cove site as commercial zoning when they should be classified as aquatic development. The Live Local Act permits developers to exceed local height and density limits only in commercial and mixed-use zones, provided they dedicate 40% of residential units to affordable housing for at least 30 years. The aquatic development zoning classification would prevent the project from utilizing Live Local Act provisions, potentially forcing developers to comply with Fort Pierce's original height and density restrictions.

 Fort Pierce City Commissioner Michael Broderick questioned whether such a significant zoning issue would have escaped state oversight during the approval process. When Trabulsy urged commissioners to rescind the project's approval and pursue legal action, Broderick expressed skepticism about the city's chances of success in court, saying he does not see an angle of attack that would not cost the city hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions of dollars, to fight.

cards.headline: Property tax increases push Treasure Coast resident to relocate to Puerto Rico
cards.teaser: A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives
cards.body:
A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives in Salinas, Puerto Rico, in a 3-bedroom home he purchased for $95,000. As a disabled veteran, he qualifies for exemptions that eliminate his property tax bill entirely.

 Tate said the price of housing in Puerto Rico is much less than Florida, especially South Florida. He said property taxes were going up and he could not afford it anymore.

 His move comes as Florida homeowners face rising property tax burdens across the state. According to a Florida Tax Watch study, property taxes rose 146.2% in St. Lucie County between 2014 and 2024. Other Treasure Coast counties saw similar increases: 131.5% in Okeechobee County, 99.4% in Palm Beach County, 90.1% in Indian River County and 90.1% in Martin County.

 Florida voters will have a chance to weigh in on property taxes this November. A referendum on the ballot would raise the Homestead Exemption, lowering property tax bills for Florida homeowners. Many city and county officials have warned that rolling back property taxes would lead to budget cuts and force local governments to raise other fees and taxes to offset lost revenue.

cards.headline: Vero Beach keeps millage flat at 2.98 mills, adds $410,000 to budget for police positions
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget
cards.body:
The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget that includes $410,000 transferred from the General Fund's unassigned fund balance to cover salaries for three vacant police officer positions. City Manager Monte Falls told the council the city holds a strong financial position with a total General Fund balance of $54 million, including $17.7 million in unassigned funds and $35.56 million in committed reserves.

 Falls recommended using $435,160 from the unassigned balance to offset the city's Other Post Employee Benefit trust payment, which would allow the vacant police positions to be filled. For a Vero Beach homeowner with a property assessed at $300,000, a $50,000 Homestead Exemption and a Save Our Homes 3 percent increase, the current millage rate would result in about $25 a year in additional ad valorem tax, Falls said.

 Vice Mayor Linda Moore and Councilmember Taylor Dingle raised concerns about funding recurring positions with non-recurring money, particularly with Amendment 3 on the November ballot potentially creating a $1.3 million budget hole. Mayor John Cotugno said Vero Beach would fare better than other Florida communities if Amendment 3 passes because the city has four enterprise funds and a diversified tax base including industrial, residential and commercial revenue sources.

 After debate, the council approved adding the $410,000 to the budget by offsetting capital expenses already included in the operating budget. Falls told Hometown News on Sept. 27 that the new police officer salaries would actually cost the city an extra $300,000. The council will return in September to set the final millage rate and adopt the budget.

The site is designated Neighborhood Village Commercial, which allows a mixture of residential and non-residential uses including commercial offices, personal and household services, institutional facilities, public facilities, parks, playgrounds and similar services. Land Use Attorney Azlina Goldstein, representing the applicant, initially resisted postponing the request and said details about landscaping, buffers and specific indoor and outdoor features would be addressed during the site-plan process, not the rezoning.

 Mayor Shannon Martin asked Goldstein if GL Homes would be willing to meet with residents to address their concerns. Vice-Mayor Jolien Caraballo urged Goldstein to table the request, saying residents did not comprehend the quasi-judicial rezoning process. After loud protest from the audience, the council voted to postpone the hearing until August 24. City Attorney Richard Berrios explained that the rezoning is a quasi-judicial process limited to sworn testimony and facts applied to the specific rezoning request, with details about landscaping and specific features reserved for the site-plan process.

cards.headline: State lawmaker challenges Fort Pierce Causeway Cove development over zoning compliance
cards.teaser: State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of the Live Local Act, raising questions about the massive waterfront project.
cards.body:
State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of Florida's Live Local Act, the same law she supported in 2023 that allows developers to bypass local height and density restrictions. The Causeway Cove project would transform the existing Causeway Cove Marina into a mixed-use development featuring more than 900 apartments and condos, restaurants, and a hotel tower reaching nearly 200 feet in height.

 Trabulsy said a mapping error incorrectly designated portions of the Causeway Cove site as commercial zoning when they should be classified as aquatic development. The Live Local Act permits developers to exceed local height and density limits only in commercial and mixed-use zones, provided they dedicate 40% of residential units to affordable housing for at least 30 years. The aquatic development zoning classification would prevent the project from utilizing Live Local Act provisions, potentially forcing developers to comply with Fort Pierce's original height and density restrictions.

 Fort Pierce City Commissioner Michael Broderick questioned whether such a significant zoning issue would have escaped state oversight during the approval process. When Trabulsy urged commissioners to rescind the project's approval and pursue legal action, Broderick expressed skepticism about the city's chances of success in court, saying he does not see an angle of attack that would not cost the city hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions of dollars, to fight.

cards.headline: Property tax increases push Treasure Coast resident to relocate to Puerto Rico
cards.teaser: A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives
cards.body:
A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives in Salinas, Puerto Rico, in a 3-bedroom home he purchased for $95,000. As a disabled veteran, he qualifies for exemptions that eliminate his property tax bill entirely.

 Tate said the price of housing in Puerto Rico is much less than Florida, especially South Florida. He said property taxes were going up and he could not afford it anymore.

 His move comes as Florida homeowners face rising property tax burdens across the state. According to a Florida Tax Watch study, property taxes rose 146.2% in St. Lucie County between 2014 and 2024. Other Treasure Coast counties saw similar increases: 131.5% in Okeechobee County, 99.4% in Palm Beach County, 90.1% in Indian River County and 90.1% in Martin County.

 Florida voters will have a chance to weigh in on property taxes this November. A referendum on the ballot would raise the Homestead Exemption, lowering property tax bills for Florida homeowners. Many city and county officials have warned that rolling back property taxes would lead to budget cuts and force local governments to raise other fees and taxes to offset lost revenue.

cards.headline: Vero Beach keeps millage flat at 2.98 mills, adds $410,000 to budget for police positions
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget
cards.body:
The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget that includes $410,000 transferred from the General Fund's unassigned fund balance to cover salaries for three vacant police officer positions. City Manager Monte Falls told the council the city holds a strong financial position with a total General Fund balance of $54 million, including $17.7 million in unassigned funds and $35.56 million in committed reserves.

 Falls recommended using $435,160 from the unassigned balance to offset the city's Other Post Employee Benefit trust payment, which would allow the vacant police positions to be filled. For a Vero Beach homeowner with a property assessed at $300,000, a $50,000 Homestead Exemption and a Save Our Homes 3 percent increase, the current millage rate would result in about $25 a year in additional ad valorem tax, Falls said.

 Vice Mayor Linda Moore and Councilmember Taylor Dingle raised concerns about funding recurring positions with non-recurring money, particularly with Amendment 3 on the November ballot potentially creating a $1.3 million budget hole. Mayor John Cotugno said Vero Beach would fare better than other Florida communities if Amendment 3 passes because the city has four enterprise funds and a diversified tax base including industrial, residential and commercial revenue sources.

 After debate, the council approved adding the $410,000 to the budget by offsetting capital expenses already included in the operating budget. Falls told Hometown News on Sept. 27 that the new police officer salaries would actually cost the city an extra $300,000. The council will return in September to set the final millage rate and adopt the budget.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce gets 90-day extension to pay state fines for Little Jim's dock violations
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection extended the city's deadline to Sept. 15 to review a proposed consent order resolving nearly $16,000 in state fines tied to docks at Little Jim Bait & Tackle.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection gave Fort Pierce until Sept. 15 to review, approve and submit a proposed consent order resolving nearly $16,000 in state fines tied to docks at Little Jim Bait & Tackle. The state agency extended the city's deadline by 90 days, meaning city commissioners have not yet formally accepted or rejected the state's enforcement terms. City staff have been negotiating with FDEP to reduce or resolve the thousands of dollars in penalties.

 The enforcement action follows allegations that the city has been operating docks at Little Jim's on state-owned submerged land without authorization. FDEP says the city never had permission to use the land. City Commissioner Michael Broderick acknowledged the allegation on July 6.

 The FDEP action is one of several legal and regulatory pressures surrounding the historic waterfront property. In early July, Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit filed by local resident Kevin Keene, who alleged years of waterfront mismanagement tied to Little Jim's. The city has filed a motion to dismiss Keene's amended complaint.

 Keene said he will continue to pursue litigation. Broderick said the city is planning to hire a real estate manager to oversee development decisions and prevent future situations.

hero.headline: Martin County firefighters rescue tree trimmer trapped 40 feet in air in Stuart
hero.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue crews on Saturday afternoon freed a tree trimmer who became trapped about 40 feet in the air after his lift stopped working in Stuart. Firefighters were d
hero.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue crews on Saturday afternoon freed a tree trimmer who became trapped about 40 feet in the air after his lift stopped working in Stuart. Firefighters were dispatched around 1 p.m. to find the man stuck on the lift, which had stopped moving up and down while he was trimming trees in the area.

 Limited access for a ladder forced crews to use a specialized high-angle rescue approach. Firefighters first removed nearby tree limbs, then used a series of high-angle rescue maneuvers to secure the man, transfer his weight and carefully bring him to the ground.

 Paramedics evaluated the man once he reached the ground and determined he had minor injuries. The man declined transportation to the hospital.

 Martin County Fire Rescue credited C-Shift crews from Heavy Rescue 23, Battalion 2, EMS 2 and EMS 22 for completing the rescue.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office warns against using social media to report crimes
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office reminded residents to call 911 for crimes in progress after an animal cruelty case was reported through social media tags.
cards.body:
Following the arrest of Ricky Lee Schieferstein on animal cruelty charges after a social media video showed alleged dog abuse, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office issued a reminder about how to report crimes. The sheriff's office said that while it appreciates the public's assistance in bringing incidents to its attention, social media platforms are not monitored continuously and should never be relied upon to report emergencies or crimes requiring an immediate law enforcement response.

 The fastest and most effective way to report a crime in progress or suspicious activity is by calling 911, according to the sheriff's office. The case began after numerous members of the community shared a video and tagged the sheriff's office across its social media platforms before the information was turned over to the criminal investigations division.

cards.headline: Costco in Stuart reopens after electrical fire with limited inventory
cards.teaser: The Costco at 3173 Kanner Highway in Stuart has reopened following an electrical fire that temporarily closed the store on Thursday. Store management told the Stuart Police Departm
cards.body:
The Costco at 3173 Kanner Highway in Stuart has reopened following an electrical fire that temporarily closed the store on Thursday. Store management told the Stuart Police Department that only dry goods are available for purchase because the refrigeration unit is not operational.

 The Stuart Police Department said the electrical fire at the Kanner Highway location has been extinguished. Shoppers and travelers were asked to avoid the area while the store was closed.

 The fire disrupted normal operations at the Martin County location. The store has since resumed limited service while the refrigeration system remains down.

 Customers visiting the Stuart Costco can purchase dry goods but will not be able to buy refrigerated or frozen items until the refrigeration unit is repaired.

cards.headline: Costco in Stuart reopens after electrical fire but refrigeration remains down
cards.teaser: The Costco at 3173 S. Kanner Highway in Stuart reopened Friday after an electrical fire forced its closure Thursday, but only dry goods are available because the refrigeration unit remains non-operational.
cards.body:
A Costco in Stuart reopened Friday with limited services after an electrical fire forced the store to close Thursday afternoon. The store at 3173 S. Kanner Highway is now open but only dry goods are available for purchase because the refrigeration unit remains non-operational, according to the Stuart Police Department.

 The electrical fire was reported at around 4 p.m. Thursday. The Stuart Police Department said out of an abundance of caution the store was closed following the fire, which was extinguished by Stuart and Martin County Fire Rescue personnel. Authorities urged individuals to avoid the area while the store remained closed Thursday.

 Store management confirmed to the Stuart Police Department that customers cannot purchase refrigerated or frozen items until the refrigeration system is restored. The police department shared the update about the limited inventory available at the location.

 The Costco location serves Stuart and surrounding Martin County communities. The store had been closed for an undetermined amount of time Thursday while fire rescue personnel remained on scene to ensure the building was safe to reopen.

cards.headline: Man charged with burglary, loitering near St. Lucie Village
cards.teaser: A 42-year-old man linked to several burglaries in the St. Lucie Village community was arrested by St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office deputies.
cards.body:
Daniel Eugene Holmes, 42, was arrested on August 5 after officers found him going through trash near the road at the 2900 block of North Indian River Drive, according to a St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office Facebook posting. During their investigation, deputies determined Holmes matched the description of a person of interest developed during an ongoing burglary investigation in St. Lucie Village. Through additional investigative efforts, deputies established probable cause linking Holmes to other reported crimes in the area.

 Holmes was charged with two counts of burglary of a conveyance and one count of loitering and prowling. He also had a bicycle with fishing equipment attached. Holmes was taken to the St. Lucie County Jail, where he remained as of August 6 on a $31,000 bond. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the case highlights the value of proactive patrol and the attention to detail deputies demonstrate every day.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police release 911 call in fatal domestic shooting of Palm Beach Sheriff's Office employee
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police released the 911 call made the night Elizabeth Ortega, 50, was shot and killed outside her home on the 2000 block of SE Oxmoor Terrace, where suspect Ralph Va
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police released the 911 call made the night Elizabeth Ortega, 50, was shot and killed outside her home on the 2000 block of SE Oxmoor Terrace, where suspect Ralph Varela Sr., 50, was later found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. In the 911 call, a neighbor described hearing five or six gunshots loud enough to rattle her house before her 4-year-old child spotted Ortega lying motionless in the front yard. The caller told the dispatcher she did not go outside because she was frightened, and that Ortega and her husband were frequently heard arguing.

 The caller said both vehicles belonging to the residents were still parked outside the home and that Ortega was not moving. Responding officers found Ortega suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. She was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died. Police said Varela returned inside the home after the shooting, where officers later found him dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

 Palm Beach Sheriff's Office said Ortega's son, Ralph Varela Jr., is a firefighter with Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, and asked the community to keep both agencies in their thoughts. The investigation remains active as detectives continue processing evidence and await final results from the Medical Examiner's Office. Funeral arrangements are pending.

 Port St. Lucie police extended their condolences to Ortega's family and loved ones. The department encouraged anyone experiencing domestic violence to ask for help and seek help.

cards.headline: Missing 14-year-old autistic boy Ethan Boyd safely located, Martin County sheriff says
cards.teaser: Ethan Boyd, a missing 14-year-old autistic boy, was safely located at 11:44 p.m., according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.
cards.body:
UPDATE — Aug. 5, 2026, 11:44 p.m.: Ethan Boyd has been safely located, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The agency announced the update in its original Facebook post and thanked the public for sharing information about the missing teenager.

 Original report: 

 The Martin County Sheriff’s Office had asked the public for help locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City. Ethan was last seen at 5:20 p.m. running toward the south side of the Grand Oaks senior living community near Coquina Cove.

 Ethan was described as 5 feet 7 inches tall, weighing approximately 130 pounds, with brown hair. He was last seen wearing a dark blue shirt and seafoam green shorts without shoes.

 The sheriff’s office asked anyone who saw Ethan to contact deputies immediately. The agency later updated its original Facebook post to announce that he had been safely located.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Kings Landing developers short $15 million, city commissioners divided on next steps
hero.teaser: The Kings Landing development in Fort Pierce faces another delay as Live Oak Development, the secondary developer on the project, told city commissioners they are $15 million short
hero.body:
The Kings Landing development in Fort Pierce faces another delay as Live Oak Development, the secondary developer on the project, told city commissioners they are $15 million short of the $60 million needed to complete the Marriott hotel and restaurant portion of the project. Live Oak Development CEO Paul Bertozzi said the shortfall is due in part to rising construction costs. City leaders said developers initially asked the city to cover the gap through a loan or grant, but Commissioner Michael Broderick said that request was denied.

 Live Oak Development is now asking for 180 days to find the money through private sources. Bertozzi told commissioners the outreach has already begun. Commissioners are debating whether the city should reclaim the property.

 Broderick said he believes trying to reclaim the property through legal action would be expensive and time-consuming. He said he would rather give developers the time they are asking for.

 Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky said he does not want to wait. Jon Nolli, owner of Funky Cuda in Fort Pierce, said he has been waiting on the development and is ready for it to be finished. Nolli said he even has plans to open businesses inside Kings Landing, including a beer garden and a deli, but the delays are wearing on him.

 The city commission has scheduled a special meeting on September 14 to discuss next steps.

cards.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce advances with luxury villas nearing completion, Marriott Hotel planned for 2029
cards.teaser: The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage,
cards.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said construction is nearly complete on Villas 9 and 10, with foundations already in place for Villas 7 and 8.

 Two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. A Marriott Hotel will be part of the development after the company signed an agreement.

 The project sits in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown Fort Pierce. Harris said the location connects downtown to Edgartown and provides walkability to shopping, restaurants, and retail. Residents with boats can store them at the marina.

 Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development could have significant impact on local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving residents a place for their families to stay. She said the downtown area will become an experience where people can walk, shop, live, and play.

 Business owners said having more residents downtown will benefit the area because most amenities are within walking distance. Chaffee Cavalcanti said people can walk to a restaurant and then go to another business to shop and get information. Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029.

cards.headline: Private racetrack resort community breaks ground in St. Lucie County on 650 acres
cards.teaser: P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fa
cards.body:
P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fall. The private racetrack resort community features 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, compared the concept to a high-end golf resort, except with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

 The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. DuPlessis said the club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels, with kids as young as 8 years old driving go-karts all the way up to grandparents still driving their cars on track, making it a family club.

 Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members. Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.

 Despite the scale of the project, developers say they want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property. DuPlessis said it will feel like the racetrack has been there for 100 years, comparing the scope of work to building a city. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

 The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

 Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island.

 City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie neighbors express concerns over commercial rezoning near Tradition
cards.teaser: Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive that is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before city council Monday.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive in Tradition that could soon be transformed from residential land to commercial use. The Port St. Lucie City Council is scheduled to hold a second reading and final vote Monday on a rezoning request that has prompted concerns from neighboring residents about overdevelopment and quality of life impacts.

 The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from a residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. According to the city, the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, though any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May.

 Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. However, Joseph Mucciolo expressed concerns about the proposed wall, saying if they put up a wall it's going to look like a prison. The couple worries that losing the open space behind their home could fundamentally alter the neighborhood character they chose when moving to the area.

 Margaret Mucciolo said they do not want over development. The family's concerns reflect broader anxieties about balancing growth with maintaining the residential quality that drew people to Tradition in the first place. Joseph Mucciolo indicated the changes could be significant enough to drive them away from their home, saying if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go.

 The rezoning proposal represents one of many land use debates facing Port St. Lucie as the city continues to grow and developers seek to convert properties to more intensive commercial uses near established residential neighborhoods.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets split doubleheader with Daytona, rally for 11-10 win in 10 innings
hero.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets split a doubleheader with the Daytona Tortugas on Wednesday at Clover Park, falling 8-4 in the opener before rallying for an 11-10 victory in 10 innings in the n
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets split a doubleheader with the Daytona Tortugas on Wednesday at Clover Park, falling 8-4 in the opener before rallying for an 11-10 victory in 10 innings in the nightcap. The twin bill made up a June 20 rainout. John Smith III delivered a two-run single in the bottom of the 10th inning, scoring Wyatt Vincent and Vladi Gomez after Daytona had taken a 10-9 lead in the top of the inning.

 The Mets forced extra innings after erasing a three-run deficit in the seventh. Gomez's two-strike, bases-loaded double tied the game 6-6 with two outs. Both teams scored in the eighth before trading two-run homers in the ninth. Daytona's Dylan King put the Tortugas ahead 9-7, but Julio Zayas answered with a game-tying two-run homer for the Mets.

 Gomez finished 4 for 5 with three doubles, two RBIs and two runs. Smith III went 2 for 5 with three RBIs, while Zayas was 3 for 4 with a home run, two RBIs and two runs scored. Daytona prospect Aaron Watson earned the win in his Single-A debut, limiting the Mets to two runs over five innings despite allowing eight hits.

 In the first game, the Tortugas took control early, capitalizing on two Mets throwing errors in the first inning before scoring four runs in the fourth, highlighted by Adolfo Sanchez's solo home run. The Mets collected 10 hits in the loss. Elian Peña went 2 for 4 with a double and two RBIs, while Aiden Robbins and Bohan Adderley each had two hits.

 Kuhio Aloy recorded the first hit of his professional career with a fifth-inning single. The Mets now stand at 14-22 in the second half and 47-55 overall, while Daytona is 23-13 and 44-58.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets fall 17-3 to Daytona as Tortugas score 11 unanswered runs at Clover Park
cards.teaser: The Daytona Tortugas scored 11 unanswered runs over the final three innings Thursday to defeat the St. Lucie Mets 17-3 at Clover Park. The Mets cut the Daytona lead to 6-3 in the f
cards.body:
The Daytona Tortugas scored 11 unanswered runs over the final three innings Thursday to defeat the St. Lucie Mets 17-3 at Clover Park. The Mets cut the Daytona lead to 6-3 in the fifth inning with three doubles, including back-to-back RBI doubles by John Smith III and Julio Zayas. The Tortugas broke the game open in the seventh inning, taking advantage of six walks issued by Mets relievers Jean Brito and Luis Sotillo to score six runs and build a 12-3 lead.

 Daytona added five more runs in the eighth inning off Zayas, who pitched the final two innings for the Mets after serving as the designated hitter. Zayas pitched a scoreless ninth inning and induced a double play. The Mets scored first on a RBI single by Reed Stallman in the second inning, but Tortugas starter Mason Morris escaped further damage with the bases loaded by starting a 1-2-3 double play off the broken bat of Kooper Schulte.

 The Tortugas used that momentum to score five runs on five hits off Mets starter Jose Lopez in the third inning. Bernard Moon hit a two-run double in the inning, his Florida State League-leading 28th double. Lopez pitched 5.1 innings overall and gave up six runs on seven hits with one walk and six strikeouts. It was the longest outing by a Mets pitcher since the first game of the second half on June 19.

 Elian Pea went 2 for 5 with a double, his third straight two-hit game. Smith III finished 2 for 4 with a double and RBI. The Mets, now 14-23 in the second half and 47-56 overall, continue their series against the Tortugas at Clover Park on Friday. All veterans and active duty military receive free admission courtesy of LYNQ Real Estate, and kids 14 and under can run the bases after the game.

cards.headline: Mets split doubleheader with Tortugas after wild 11-10 walk-off win
cards.teaser: John Smith III lined a two-run single in the bottom of the 10th inning as St. Lucie erased a late deficit and beat Daytona 11-10 after dropping the opener.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets split a doubleheader with the Daytona Tortugas at Clover Park on Wednesday night, dropping the opener 8-4 before rallying for a dramatic 11-10 victory in 10 innings in Game 2.

 John Smith III ended the nearly six-hour twin bill with a two-run, walk-off single in the bottom of the 10th. The victory kept St. Lucie from being swept in a doubleheader for the fourth time this season and snapped Daytona’s season-high seven-game winning streak.

 The doubleheader was scheduled to make up a June 20 rainout between the teams.

 Daytona took a 10-9 lead in the top of the 10th inning of Game 2 when Rafhlmil Torres delivered a two-out RBI single. Mets reliever Tyler McLoughlin prevented any further damage, giving St. Lucie a chance to answer in the bottom half.

 Vladi Gomez opened the inning with a bunt single, putting runners at the corners. After a strikeout, the Tortugas intentionally walked Elian Peña to load the bases. Smith then lined a two-strike pitch into right field, scoring Wyatt Vincent and Gomez to give the Mets the win.

 St. Lucie had already erased a three-run deficit in the seventh inning. The Mets trailed 6-3 with two outs and the bases loaded when Gomez doubled into left field. Bernard Moon overran the ball, allowing a third run to score and tying the game 6-6.

 Both teams scored their automatic runner in the eighth. Drew Davies drew a bases-loaded walk from Ernesto Mercedes to put Daytona ahead 7-6, but Jesus Colina threw a wild pitch with two outs in the bottom of the inning, allowing Kooper Schulte to score from third and tie the game again.

 The teams traded two-run home runs in the ninth. Dylan King homered off Mercedes to give the Tortugas a 9-7 lead, but Julio Zayas answered with a leadoff, two-run homer against Colina in the bottom half to make it 9-9.

 Gomez finished Game 2 4-for-5 with three doubles, two RBIs and two runs. Smith went 2-for-5 with a double and three RBIs. Zayas was 3-for-4 with a home run, two singles, a walk, two RBIs and two runs.

 Daytona controlled Game 1 from the start. Tortugas starter Aaron Watson, the Cincinnati Reds’ No. 5 prospect, made his Single-A debut and held the Mets to two runs over five innings.

 The Mets collected eight hits against Watson but stranded seven runners. Watson escaped a bases-loaded jam in the third by retiring Ryan Stallman, then induced Aiden Robbins into an inning-ending double play with runners at the corners in the fourth.

 The Tortugas scored twice in the first inning after Arnaldo Lantigua singled and the Mets committed two throwing errors on the play. Daytona broke the game open with four runs in the fourth. Adolfo Sanchez hit a solo home run, two more runs scored on a throwing error by Peña at shortstop and Davies added an RBI double off Conner Ware to make it 6-1.

 Daytona scored its final two runs against Caden Wooster on a wild pitch and a solo home run by Lantigua.

 The Mets finished with 10 hits in the loss. Peña went 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs, while Robbins and Bohan Adderley each went 2-for-4. Kuhio Aloy, an 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, recorded the first hit of his professional career with a fifth-inning single and also drew a walk.

 Will Watson made a rehab start for St. Lucie and pitched the first inning. He was charged with two unearned runs and took the loss.

 The Mets moved to 14-22 in the second half and 47-55 overall. The Tortugas are 23-13 in the second half and 44-58 overall.

 St. Lucie and Daytona are scheduled to play a single nine-inning game Thursday at Clover Park. First pitch is set for 6:10 p.m. The promotion is $2 Night, with select beer, hot dogs, fountain soda and popcorn available for $2.

cards.headline: PSL Mets score three in 10th to beat Blue Jays 6-3
cards.teaser: John Smith III reached base four times and scored a key insurance run as St. Lucie snapped a three-game losing streak with an extra-inning win in Dunedin.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets scored three runs in the 10th inning Saturday night to defeat the Dunedin Blue Jays 6-3 at TD Ballpark.

 The extra-inning victory snapped St. Lucie’s three-game losing streak and improved the Mets to 3-1 in extra-inning games this season. Dunedin rallied twice during regulation to tie the game but never took the lead.

 Ryan Tayman opened the scoring with a two-run double in the first inning, giving St. Lucie an early 2-0 advantage. JoJo Parker tied the game with a two-run home run in the sixth.

 The Mets regained the lead in the seventh when Elian Peña scored on a two-out RBI infield single by John Smith III.

 St. Lucie carried a 3-2 lead into the bottom of the ninth, but the Blue Jays loaded the bases with no outs against Elwis Mijares. Zack Mack entered from the bullpen and limited Dunedin to a sacrifice fly, sending the game to extra innings tied 3-3.

 Peña advanced to third on a wild pitch by Noah Palmese in the top of the 10th before Wyatt Vincent delivered a sacrifice fly to put the Mets back in front.

 Smith III was then hit by a pitch and later scored on another Palmese wild pitch, extending the lead to 5-3. Julio Zayas followed with an RBI single to bring home St. Lucie’s final run.

 Mack retired the Blue Jays in the bottom of the 10th and induced a game-ending groundout from Jake Cook, who represented the potential tying run. Mack earned the victory after pitching two scoreless innings.

 Smith III finished 2-for-3 with two singles, a walk and a hit-by-pitch. He drove in one run, scored twice and reached base in four of his five plate appearances.

 Mets starter Nate Hall allowed one hit over three scoreless innings and recorded one strikeout. Jonathan Jimenez added 2⅓ scoreless innings with four strikeouts.

 The Mets improved to 13-21 in the second half and 46-54 overall. The Blue Jays fell to 17-17 in the second half and 47-52 overall.

 St. Lucie and Dunedin will conclude their six-game series Sunday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for noon, with the Mets seeking their second 3-3 series split of the season.

cards.headline: Blue Jays score five in eighth to shut out St. Lucie Mets 5-0
cards.teaser: Ethan Lanthier and Christian Rodriguez held Dunedin scoreless through seven innings, but the Blue Jays broke through with five runs in the eighth to hand St. Lucie its third straight loss in the series.
cards.body:
DUNEDIN — A scoreless pitchers' duel unraveled for the St. Lucie Mets in the eighth inning Friday night as the Dunedin Blue Jays scored five runs and pulled away for a 5-0 victory at TD Ballpark.

 The loss was St. Lucie's third straight in the series. The Mets kept Dunedin off the scoreboard through seven innings behind strong outings from starter Ethan Lanthier and reliever Christian Rodriguez, but the Blue Jays sent eight batters to the plate during the decisive eighth.

 Lanthier delivered four scoreless innings, allowing one hit. Rodriguez followed with three hitless frames before running into trouble in his fourth inning of work.

 The eighth began when Rodriguez walked No. 9 hitter Brayden Martin, who reached on walks in all three of his plate appearances. Rodriguez then hit Jake Cook with a pitch. Blaine Bullard and Ryan Cooney followed with consecutive RBI singles to give Dunedin a 2-0 lead.

 With two outs, Jake Bennett doubled over the first-base bag to drive in two more runs. Enmanuel Bonilla scored from third on a wild pitch to complete the five-run inning.

 Rodriguez was charged with five runs on three hits over four innings and took the loss.

 Dunedin starter Carson Messina struck out seven over a season-high 4 2/3 innings without issuing a walk. Reese Bassinger retired all four batters he faced, Landen Waters worked a perfect seventh and Josbel Garcia pitched the final two innings to complete the shutout and earn the win.

 The Mets finished with five hits from five players. Simon Juan went 1-for-4 with a triple, while Aiden Robbins reached base three times with a single, a walk and a hit-by-pitch.

 St. Lucie fell to 12-21 in the second half and 45-54 overall. Dunedin improved to 17-16 in the second half and 47-51 overall.

 The teams continue the series Saturday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Blue Jays outlast St. Lucie Mets 14-9 in Dunedin slugfest
cards.teaser: Yovanny Rodriguez and Bohan Adderley hit their first St. Lucie home runs, but Dunedin scored six unanswered runs after the Mets briefly took a 9-8 lead.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets hit three home runs and briefly rallied into the lead Wednesday night, but the Dunedin Blue Jays scored six unanswered runs over the final three innings to win 14-9 at TD Ballpark.

 The loss evened the series at one game apiece. St. Lucie has scored 51 runs over its last five games but has allowed 52, going 2-3 during that stretch.

 Yovanny Rodriguez gave the Mets a 3-0 lead in the first inning with a three-run homer, his first since joining St. Lucie from the Florida Complex League.

 Dunedin answered quickly. JoJo Parker hit a two-run homer off Owen Woodward in the bottom of the first, then connected for another two-run shot against Jose Lopez in the second. Parker, the Blue Jays’ top prospect, finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk, four RBIs and four runs scored.

 St. Lucie trailed 8-6 entering the fifth before Simon Juan and Bohan Adderley hit back-to-back home runs with two outs. Juan’s two-run shot tied the game, and Adderley followed with his first St. Lucie homer to put the Mets ahead 9-8.

 The lead held until the seventh, when Dunedin scored four runs against reliever Zack Mack. Parker opened the rally with a hard infield single that first baseman Branny De Oleo stopped, but De Oleo’s throw toward second base escaped into the outfield and allowed Jake Cook to score the tying run.

 Juan Sanchez then chopped a two-run single to give the Blue Jays an 11-9 lead and later scored on a wild pitch. Dunedin added two more runs in the eighth on RBI singles by Brayden Martin and Blaine Bullard.

 After Adderley’s go-ahead homer, Dunedin relievers Noah Palmese, Ricky Tiedemann, Isaac Williams and Dax Dathe combined to retire 10 consecutive Mets batters.

 Elian Peña ended that streak with a leadoff single in the ninth and reached third on an error with no outs. The Mets had a chance to score in double figures for a fourth consecutive game, but Bradley Wilson struck out three straight batters to strand Peña at third.

 Peña went 2-for-4 with two singles and two RBIs, while Adderley finished 2-for-4. Eight of St. Lucie’s nine starters recorded at least one hit.

 Dylan Carey, an undrafted free agent from Nebraska, made his professional debut and went 1-for-3 with a single, a hit-by-pitch and a run scored. He also played error-free defense at shortstop.

 Elwis Mijares provided the strongest outing from the Mets bullpen, pitching 2⅓ scoreless innings with three strikeouts. Woodward, pitching on a minor league rehabilitation assignment, worked the first inning and ended his appearance with consecutive strikeouts.

 Lopez followed Woodward and allowed six runs on four hits and six walks over 2⅔ innings. Mack took the loss after being charged with four runs in two-thirds of an inning.

 Sanchez finished 2-for-4 with a double, two walks and four RBIs for Dunedin. Cook reached base in each of his final five plate appearances with three singles and two walks.

 The Mets fell to 12-19 in the second half and 45-52 overall. The Blue Jays improved to 14-17 in the second half and 45-51 overall.

 The teams play the third game of the series Thursday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
cards.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
cards.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

 Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

 The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

 Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

 Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

 Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

 The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

 Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

 Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

 Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

 Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

 The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

 Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

 The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

 The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Space Coast Symphony Orchestra brings Landscapes & Legends concert to Vero Beach
cards.teaser: The Space Coast Symphony Orchestra will perform Landscapes Legends on Sunday, August 10, at the Community Church of Vero Beach, 1901 23rd Street. The concert features works explori
cards.body:
The Space Coast Symphony Orchestra will perform Landscapes Legends on Sunday, August 10, at the Community Church of Vero Beach, 1901 23rd Street. The concert features works exploring magic and myth, with guest conductor Patrick Phillips leading the performance.

 The program opens with Dukas' The Sorcerer's Apprentice, the 11-minute orchestral tone poem famously depicted in Disney's Fantasia. The concert includes the world premiere performance of Kenneth Fuchs' Cloud Slant, a work capturing light, motion and atmosphere. Fuchs won the 2018 GRAMMY Award for Best Classical Compendium for an album recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra for Naxos.

 Vero Beach music and arts leader Dr. Jacob Craig will perform Edward MacDowell's Piano Concerto No. 2, a deeply romantic and expressive three-movement work composed in 1885. The work holds the distinction of being the first major piano concerto written by an American. Renowned pianist Van Cliburn chose MacDowell's Piano Concerto No. 2 at age 18 for his professional orchestral debut.

 The concert concludes with Pines of Rome, the 1924 orchestral tone poem by Italian composer Ottorino Respighi. The 22-minute work dramatically depicts four different locations around Rome framed by iconic pine trees. Tickets cost $35 through www.SpaceCoastSymphony.org or at Marine Bank Trust branches, and $40 at the door.

 Concertgoers aged 18 and under or with a college ID are admitted free. For more information, call 855-252-7276.

cards.teaser: More than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, John Singer Sargent and Mary Cassatt are on display at Vero Beach Museum of Art through Aug. 16.
cards.body:
An exhibition titled American Made at Vero Beach Museum of Art includes more than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, Sarah Miriam Peale, Edward Moran, John Singer Sargent, Mary Cassatt, Robert Henri and Charles Alston. The exhibit runs through Aug. 16 at the Holmes and Titelman Galleries at 3001 Riverside Park Drive in Vero Beach.

 Another exhibit, James Prosek: At Work, is on display at the museum's Holmes Gallery through Oct. 25. The exhibit features projects which define the artist's first 30 years of artmaking. Admission is free to members, children 17 and younger, and military veterans and active duty military with valid ID. Admission is $12 for adults, $11 for seniors and $5 for students with ID.

 The museum is also displaying Envisioning the New VBMA, an exhibit tracing the evolution of designs for the museum's new building and transformed campus created by Allied Works architecture and Unknown Studio Landscape Architecture Urban Design. That exhibit runs through Jan. 3, 2027.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for October 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart.
